Re: Appeal of Medical-Necessity Denial  
Member: Rowan Lawson  
Member ID: W383949058  
Reference number: POC-F37F115FED-48372  
Requested service: Lumbar disc surgery/decompression  
CPT: 63030  
Date of denial notice: August 23, 2026

To Anthem Appeals:

I am appealing Anthem’s denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, lumbar disc surgery/decompression. The denial states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria. I request that Anthem overturn the denial and authorize the procedure.

The clinical record supports the medical necessity of surgery:

- I have had 24 months of progressive lower-back pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 18 supervised physical-therapy visits over 10 weeks, from April 20, 2026, through June 29, 2026. Treatment included core stabilization and lumbar-flexibility exercises, without adequate relief.
- I used NSAIDs for six months without adequate improvement.
- A corticosteroid injection on April 13, 2026, produced only two weeks of partial relief.
- MRI on June 30, 2026, showed an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral-recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- My symptoms correspond to that imaging: radicular pain extends into the right calf, and I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes.
- Examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.
- The requested procedure is directed at the documented L4-L5 pathology and L5 nerve-root compression.

The available clinical information therefore establishes a confirmed structural diagnosis, a clear clinical and imaging correlation, persistent and function-limiting symptoms, failure of extended conservative treatment, and a reasonable basis to expect that decompression will improve function and relieve nerve-root symptoms. The anticipated benefit of treating the documented nerve-root compression outweighs the risks of continued symptoms and delay.

The records also document the absence of relevant contraindicating concerns: there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, and I am a nonsmoker. My BMI is 29.

I have not quoted Anthem’s governing policy because the denial notice does not identify the policy or clinical-review document used for this determination. The publicly available material reviewed includes a general spine-surgery guideline, but it does not establish that the guideline governed this Georgia Anthem commercial/ACA determination. Please provide the exact policy or clinical-review criteria applied to this request, including the document title, policy number, version or effective date, and the specific reasons the submitted records allegedly failed those criteria.

Please conduct a new review using the enclosed records and authorize CPT 63030. If Anthem continues to deny authorization, please provide a detailed explanation identifying each unmet criterion, the clinical information relied upon, the reviewing clinician’s specialty, and instructions for any external review available under the plan.

This appeal is submitted before the February 19, 2027 deadline stated in the denial notice.

Enclosures:

- Denial notice dated August 23, 2026
- MRI report dated June 30, 2026
- Physical-therapy discharge note documenting 18 visits from April 20, 2026, through June 29, 2026
- Medication and conservative-treatment history
- Corticosteroid-injection record dated April 13, 2026
- Orthopedic examination and neurologic findings
- Surgeon’s clinical documentation and request for CPT 63030

Please send the appeal determination and the requested policy or clinical-review criteria to:

Rowan Lawson
